'''Hubert Curien''' (30 October 1924 – 6 February 2005) was a French [[physicist]] and a key figure in European science politics, as the President of [[List of presidents of the CERN Council|CERN Council]] (1994–1996),<ref>{{cite web|title=CERN prepares its Future|url=http://press.web.cern.ch/press-releases/1993/06/cern-prepares-its-future|website=CERN Press Office|publisher=CERN}}</ref> the first chairman of the [[European Space Agency]] (ESA) (1981–1984), and second President of the [[Academia Europæa]] and a President of [[Fondation de France]].

==Biography==
Born in [[Cornimont]], [[Vosges (department)|Vosges]] in [[Lorraine (region)|Lorraine]], Curien enlisted in the French resistance during [[World War II]]. After the war he studied physics at the [[École normale supérieure (Paris)|École normale supérieure]] in Paris.

Curien became the director general of the [[Centre national de la recherche scientifique|Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique]] (CNRS) in 1969, and was one of the founders of the [[European Science Foundation]] and chairman from 1979 to 1984. He was also head of the French space agency from 1976 to 1984, and first chairman of the board of ESA from 1981 to 1984.

Curien was the Minister of Research of France from 1984 to 1986 and from 1988 to 1993. He entered the [[French Academy of Sciences]] in 1994.<ref>[http://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/WAspad/UnTexteDeJorf?numjo=RESM9400045D Decree of February 9, 1994, approving the election of Hubert Curien to the Academy of sciences]</ref>

Curien was the President of the [[Fondation de France]] from 1998 through 2000.

Two years later, in November 2002, he retired from [[CERN]] after 38 years of contribution to accelerator projects, starting as a fellow in 1964.<ref>{{cite journal|title=People|journal=CERN Courier|date=January 2003|volume=43|issue=1|page=42|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/1733427}}</ref>

As a tribute to Curien, the French Ministry of Foreign Affairs has decided to rename its bilateral scientific exchange programmes, previously referred to as "Integrated Action Programmes" or "PAI" to "Hubert Curien Partnerships" or "PHC". The French Ministry of Foreign Affairs has such "Hubert Curien Partnerships" with more than 60 countries of the world.

The 2004 Forum Engelberg also paid tribute to their President Curien for the occasion of his upcoming 80th birthday.<ref>{{cite journal|title=People: Forum Engelberg pays tribute to Curien|journal=CERN Courier|date=May 2004|volume=44|issue=4|page=33|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/1733625}}</ref>

In honor of his contribution to European space, it was decided by ESA, NASA, and the international Committee for Space Research ([[COSPAR]]) to name the landing site of the [[Huygens probe]] after him, and from 14 March 2007 it is known as the "Hubert Curien Memorial Station".<ref>[http://sci.esa.int/science-e/www/object/index.cfm?fobjectid=40807 ESA News item dated 06 Mar 2007, Huygens landing site to be named after Hubert Curien]</ref>

His son [[Pierre-Louis Curien]] is a noted theoretical computer scientist.
